lesson.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run root endpoint
steps.instructions: Install fastapi and uvicorn with pip, then create main.py with a FastAPI app and a root GET route. Run the server with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and openin your browser.

targets.caption: Define the root GET endpoint in main.py

hints: Make sure both fastapi and uvicorn are installed in your active Python environment.
In main.py, instantiate app = FastAPI() and decorate a function with @app.get("/").
Run uvicorn main:app --reload from the directory containing main.py.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to install uvicorn separately when running pip install fastapi.
Running uvicorn from a different folder than main.py or misspelling main:app.

steps.title: Add POST /items endpoint
steps.instructions: Create main.py with `app = FastAPI()`, an empty `items` list and a POST /items endpoint that appends the `item` query string and returns the list, then start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload`. From a second terminal, run `curl -X POST ''` to add an item.

explanations.topic: Accepting a query parameter on a POST route

hints: Initialize items = [] above your route handlers so items persist in memory.
Use @app.post("/items") with def create_item(item: str): and append to items.
Send a POST request with ?item=apple in the URL using curl.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to keep the uvicorn --reload server running in the first terminal.

steps.title: Add GET /items/{item_id} route
steps.instructions: In main.py, add a GET /items/{item_id} endpoint that takes an integer item_id path parameter and returns items[item_id]. With uvicorn main:app --reload running, re-add an item via your POST endpoint, then request item 0 with curl against your local server on port 8000.

targets.caption: Define path parameter route for a single item
Server log of the item request

explanations.topic: In-memory list resets on uvicorn reload
Path parameter type conversion with int

hints: Put {item_id} in the route string and item_id: int in the function signature.
Because uvicorn --reload clears the items list on save, POST at least one item before testing GET.
common_mistakes: Testing GET /items/0 right after editing main.py without re-adding items via POST.
Omitting the int type hint on item_id, which leaves it as a string and causes a TypeError.

steps.title: Return 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: In main.py, import HTTPException from fastapi and make get_item raise a 404 HTTPException when item_id is out of range. With uvicorn running, curl a missing item ID such as /items/3.

targets.caption: Raise a 404 error when item_id does not exist

explanations.topic: HTTP 404 status codes for missing resources
Using HTTPException with status_code and detail

hints: Import HTTPException alongside FastAPI at the top of main.py.
Check if item_id < len(items): before indexing into items.
Use raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found") in the else branch.
common_mistakes: Returning HTTPException instead of raising it with the raise keyword.
Forgetting to import HTTPException from fastapi.

steps.title: Add GET /items list with limit
steps.instructions: Add a GET /items endpoint in main.py with an optional `limit: int = 10` query parameter returning `items[0:limit]`. Re-add several items via POST, then run `curl ''` and also without the limit.

targets.caption: Define GET /items with a default query parameter

explanations.topic: Query parameters with default values and type conversion

hints: Define @app.get("/items") with def list_items(limit: int = 10):.
Slice the list with return items[0:limit].
Test both /items?limit=3 and /items after posting items to the server.
common_mistakes: Omitting the = 10 default value, making limit mandatory on GET /items.
Forgetting quotes around the URL when passing query parameters in zsh or bash.

steps.title: Validate payloads with Pydantic BaseModel
steps.instructions: In main.py, import BaseModel from pydantic and define an Item model with text: str and is_done: bool = False. Use Item in create_item and get_item, then POST a JSON body with curl.

explanations.topic: Why use Pydantic models in FastAPI
JSON request body vs query parameters
Making fields required by removing default None

hints: Import BaseModel using from pydantic import BaseModel.
Remove = None from text: str so FastAPI validates that text is always provided.
Pass the item as JSON with -d '{"text":"apple"}' in curl instead of a query parameter.
common_mistakes: Still sending ?item=apple as a query parameter after switching item to a Pydantic model.
Leaving text: str = None when you want text to be required.

steps.title: Add response_model to GET routes
steps.instructions: In main.py, add response_model=list[Item] to the GET /items decorator and response_model=Item to the GET /items/{item_id} decorator.

targets.caption: Declare the response model on the list route
Declare the response model on the single-item route

hints: Pass response_model as a keyword argument inside @app.get(...).
Use response_model=list[Item] for list_items and response_model=Item for get_item.
common_mistakes: Putting response_model inside the function parameters instead of the @app.get decorator.

steps.title: Test API in Swagger interactive docs
steps.instructions: Open the /docs page of your running server in Chrome, expand POST /items, click Try it out, enter a JSON item body, and click Execute.

targets.caption: Click Try it out and Execute on POST /items
Send the request from the docs

explanations.topic: Alternative ReDoc and OpenAPI JSON schema

hints: Expand the green POST /items section and click the Try it out button.
Provide a JSON object with a "text" string field and click Execute.
common_mistakes: Leaving invalid JSON syntax (such as trailing commas) in the Request body editor.
Sending a request without a text field when text is required on Item.
